preamble: Centralization and lowering of the close back rounded vowel [u] to the close-mid central rounded [ɵ]. In Swedish, Old Norse short u that stayed short is now /ɵ/, as in Old Norse hundr 'dog' > hund /hɵnd/ and ungr 'young' > ung /ɵŋː/. The Old Norse article's table of vowel developments gives Old Norse u > Swedish ɵ/ʉː ⟨u⟩, that is short [ɵ] and long [ʉː], since vowel length in Swedish now follows syllable structure. Old Swedish long ū became [ʉː] in the Late Old Swedish vowel shift (hūs > hus [hʉːs]), listed under u → ʉ. Swedish phonology treats short /ɵ/ and long /ʉː/ as a pair that differs in quality as well as length (full /fɵl/ 'full', ful /fʉːl/ 'ugly'): it cites Engstrand (1990) for a mid [ɵ̞] and Persson (2024) for a near-close /ɵ/ in contemporary Stockholm speech.

examples.note: Wikipedia's Swedish phonology writes /fɵl/, without marking the long consonant.

examples.note: The same Old Norse u is near-close [ʏ] in Icelandic (fullur [ˈfʏtlʏr]) and a back [ʊ] in Faroese.
